citation.title: Pragmatic generative optimization of novel structural lattice metamaterials with machine learning
citation.authors: Anthony P. Garland, Benjamin C. White, Scott C. Jensen, Brad L. Boyce
citation.venue: Materials & Design 203 (2021) 109632 (Elsevier; publication date 2021-03-02 per OpenAlex; gold open access, CC BY per OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar metadata; OSTI record 1768685)
citation.version_coded: none: abstract only (OpenAlex abstract as stored in the pool); full text not reachable

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (abstract only). The abstract says an ML-guided search finds Pareto-optimal lattice unit cells for stiffness under static load and low wave speed under impact, with about 3500 simulation calls. It names no classical comparator.

notes: Access attempts on 2026-09-24, all anonymous with the generic User-Agent. (6) OSTI 1841074 (SAND2021-0287C) is the first author's conference slides, not the article; they were read for context only and are not coded. The slides describe a CNN surrogate for modulus and wave speed on a 12x12-pixel unit cell, used inside an NSGA-II genetic algorithm with active learning over 11 generations. Their results compare with intuition-based designs and 15k random designs; a slide on design methods argues that TO does not suit contact and failure. [inferred from the slides, not the article: the full text may hold no classical-optimizer comparison, so FT-NOBASELINE or FT-MLONLY is a plausible outcome; the verifier should check.] Scope note: one objective is wave speed through the lattice during an impact event (explicit dynamics with contact per the slides). This is impact-wave, not acoustic or phononic design, but the verifier may treat elastic-wave objectives as the open FT-DOMAIN (acoustic) scope question. Free to read in a browser: yes, the version of record is gold open access (CC BY) at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521001854, so a human can fetch and code it. method_family cnn rests on the slides and a search-engine summary of the article, not on the article text.
